sentences.text: S2 stated that her mother, Margaret (81 years old), has dementia diagnosed two years ago and lives at Larch Road with carers.
S2 stated that her brother, Martin, holds the power of attorney for financial and property affairs, which was signed by Margaret in 2023 and registered.
S2 stated that she found a £12,000 transfer from Margaret's account to Martin's account on 14 August.
S2 stated that Martin arrived at Margaret's house in a new white estate car in early September.
S2 stated that when asked where the money came from, Martin claimed Margaret had 'helped him out' and that he was entitled to it because he does everything for her.
S2 stated that there is no known gift from Margaret to Martin prior to her dementia.
S2 stated that on 22 September, Margaret told her that Martin made her sign something, though Margaret did not know what it was and was frightened to say no.
S2 stated that she has not seen the document Margaret was told was signed on 22 September, having looked in her drawers with no result.
S2 stated that Margaret's care invoices from Brightwell are three months behind, with a debt of approximately £2,400.
S2 stated that Brightwell wrote to Margaret's address on 3 November warning that calls might stop if the debt is not paid.
S2 stated that Margaret has a social worker (whom S2 has never met) and a GP at the Wexley health centre.
S2 stated that she is worried about Margaret's house being sold, which would leave nothing for her care.
S2 stated that Martin has not yet said anything about selling the house.
S2 stated she felt better after telling someone.
S2 stated that she has photos of the bank statements on her phone and has printed copies.
S2 stated that she has the letter from Brightwell dated 3 November.
S2 stated that she wants Margaret's money protected and wants Martin unable to touch it.
S2 stated that she is worried about the house being sold.
S1 advised that an attorney must act in the client's best interests and keep money separate.
S1 advised that a £12,000 transfer to the attorney without authority is something the Office of the Public Guardian will investigate.
S1 advised that the Office of the Public Guardian can ask the attorney to account for money and apply to the Court of Protection to cancel the power of attorney.
S1 advised that taking money as an attorney can be a criminal offence.
S1 advised that Margaret is an adult at risk and recommended an adult safeguarding referral to Wexley council.
S1 advised S2 not to confront Martin about the matter for now, as it could cause him to move more money or become defensive.
S1 advised S2 to ring Brightwell to explain the situation is in hand so calls do not stop.
S1 instructed S2 to email the statement photos and the agency letter by Friday 27th.
S1 instructed S2 that he would write to the Office of the Public Guardian by Tuesday 1st December.
S1 instructed S2 that he would make the safeguarding referral today.
S1 instructed S2 to send the client care letter today.
S1 scheduled a next meeting for 8th December.
